Since the labels are known up front, Quail stores them in a trie and constrains decoding to paths in the trie. Quail stops decoding as soon as only one label is left, instead of decoding the full label. Quail also packs these few decode steps into the same forward passes as the prefill of other documents, so the GPU stays busy. 

On 12 classification queries, Quail is ~1.8x faster than a vLLM baseline!

由于标签是预先已知的，Quail 会将它们存储在 trie 中，并将解码限制在 trie 的路径内。Quail 不会解码完整标签，而是在只剩下一个标签时立即停止解码。Quail 还会把这几步解码打包进其他文档预填充的同一批前向传播中，让 GPU 保持忙碌。

在 12 个分类查询上，Quail 比 vLLM 基线快约 1.8 倍！

posts.text: SSMs had the nice asymptotics but kept missing out on the inference goodies Transformers get for free like spec decode and quantization. Turns out we were just not caching the right thing. Same IO-aware trick behind FlashAttention, Mamba scan, paged KV. A lot of the big wins weren’t new architectures, just people taking memory IO seriously.

quotedTweet.text:
ReplaySSM now runs in production in GLM-5.3-Flash and Kimi-K3, and ships in TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, FlashInfer, and SGLang!

It speeds up standard decoding (up to 1.47x) and speculative decoding (up to 2.1x), and now also enables a low-precision SSM state whose rounding error never propagates through the recurrence.

Building on our earlier ReplaySSM work, we collaborated with @NVIDIA to pin down what the method really unlocks. Caching SSM inputs instead of the state is what ReplaySSM does. What it changes is that computing the output and updating the state can be separated during decoding. All three gains follow from that separation.

Joint blog post, paper, and code with @NVIDIA and @tri_dao 👇
quotedTweet.translationZh:
ReplaySSM 现在已在 GLM-5.3-Flash 和 Kimi-K3 的生产环境中运行，并已集成到 TensorRT-LLM、vLLM、FlashInfer 和 SGLang 中！

它能加速标准解码（最高 1.47 倍）和推测解码（最高 2.1 倍），现在还支持低精度 SSM 状态，其舍入误差永远不会通过递归传播。

在我们此前 ReplaySSM 工作的基础上，我们与 @NVIDIA 合作，明确了这一方法真正释放的能力。ReplaySSM 做的是缓存 SSM 输入而不是状态。它带来的变化是，在解码期间可以将输出计算与状态更新分离。所有三项收益都源于这种分离。

与 @NVIDIA 和 @tri_dao 联合发布的博客、论文和代码 👇

posts.text:
两个今天能力差不多的 Agent，跑上一段时间后，可能会拉开非常大的差距。

Meta 等团队这篇《Agent Plasticity》，想测的就是一件事：

Agent 到底有多会「从经验里变强」。

作者让模型权重保持不变，只允许 Agent 根据过去的成功和失败，持续修改自己的 Memory、Skills、策略和 Python 工具。

然后每隔一段时间，用全新的任务测试它，看这些经验有没有真正留下来。

论文提出了一个指标叫「Agent Plasticity」：

既看 Agent 最终提升了多少，也看为了获得这些提升花了多少学习成本。

实验覆盖 Chess、Go、Hex 和 NetHack。结果是不同前沿模型即使拿到类似的反馈和学习机会，自我改进曲线也差得非常大。

比如 Claude Fable 5 最终能力最高，但 GPT-5.6 Sol 的「学习效率」反而更高。

还有一些模型反复积累经验，表现几乎没涨，甚至下降。

进一步分析发现，弱自我改进 Agent 的一个典型问题，是明明已经存下了相关 Skill 和 Memory，执行时却根本想不起来用；而更强的 Agent 即使用上经验，也还会遇到经验质量和泛化的问题。

所以我觉得「Agent 有多强」和「Agent 有多会学习」以后可能会变成两个完全不同的指标。

真正的自进化能力，看的可能不只是一次 benchmark 能拿多少分，而是经历 10 次、100 次任务之后，它能不能把踩过的坑稳定变成下一次的能力。

BREAKING: 🇫🇷 A major cyberattack has hit supermarket refrigeration systems across France, reportedly causing fresh and frozen food to spoil after hackers remotely manipulated temperature controls.

According to BFMTV, the attack began overnight from Sunday into Monday, targeting older versions of refrigeration-control software supplied by Danish company Danfoss.

The attackers allegedly exploited the systems’ defrosting function, forcing refrigeration equipment to heat continuously instead of keeping products cold. Temperatures were reportedly set as high as 50°C, destroying entire stocks of food within hours.

Several major supermarket chains have been affected, including Intermarché, Super U and https://t.co/7bHBi61WPZ. Metro stores and independent businesses, including butcher shops also have been impacted.

Around 150 Intermarché stores are reportedly affected, according to industry sources cited by BFMTV. The full number of affected locations remains unclear.

The financial damage is already significant. In Haguenau, Alsace, an Intermarché store reportedly lost its entire frozen-food stock, worth approximately €50,000. A nearby Super U allegedly had to discard both fresh and frozen products, with losses estimated at €220,000. An https://t.co/7bHBi61WPZ store in the same town was also affected, although its losses had not yet been calculated.

The combined losses reported at the Intermarché and Super U stores in Haguenau alone amount to around €270,000. Nationwide damage could reach several million euros.

Intermarché reportedly confirmed the incident in an internal communication, warning that several stores had suffered losses of frozen products. Coopérative U also acknowledged the attack and established crisis teams to assist affected stores and coordinate with refrigeration specialists.

Technical investigations are ongoing, and the full extent of the damage has yet to be established.

Authorities and companies are still working to determine the full circumstances of the attack. The identity of the perpetrators has not been confirmed.

New blog post with @charles_irl on how Quail classifies documents with LLMs ~1.8x faster than baselines!! https://t.co/42QNTsdmv8

reviewedPosts.author: Xudong07452910
reviewedPosts.text:
两个今天能力差不多的 Agent，跑上一段时间后，可能会拉开非常大的差距。

Meta 等团队这篇《Agent Plasticity》，想测的就是一件事：

Agent 到底有多会「从经验里变强」。

作者让模型权重保持不变，只允许 Agent 根据过去的成功和失败，持续修改自己的 Memory、Skills、策略和 Python 工具。

然后每隔一段时间，用全新的任务测试它，看这些经验有没有真正留下来。

论文提出了一个指标叫「Agent Plasticity」：

既看 Agent 最终提升了多少，也看为了获得这些提升花了多少学习成本。

实验覆盖 Chess、Go、Hex 和 NetHack。结果是不同前沿模型即使拿到类似的反馈和学习机会，自我改进曲线也差得非常大。

比如 Claude Fable 5 最终能力最高，但 GPT-5.6 Sol 的「学习效率」反而更高。

还有一些模型反复积累经验，表现几乎没涨，甚至下降。

进一步分析发现，弱自我改进 Agent 的一个典型问题，是明明已经存下了相关 Skill 和 Memory，执行时却根本想不起来用；而更强的 Agent 即使用上经验，也还会遇到经验质量和泛化的问题。

所以我觉得「Agent 有多强」和「Agent 有多会学习」以后可能会变成两个完全不同的指标。

真正的自进化能力，看的可能不只是一次 benchmark 能拿多少分，而是经历 10 次、100 次任务之后，它能不能把踩过的坑稳定变成下一次的能力。

📎 arxiv: https://t.co/VxSQ3o4EB8

这篇我很推荐，尤其是现在做科研的人。

作者 Pierre Marion 提了一个很有意思的判断。LLM 如果真的把算公式、写代码、搜文献、做实验这些环节加速 10 倍甚至 100 倍，科研里最稀缺的东西会慢慢转向选什么问题、怎么建模、以及怎么判断结果有没有价值。

更值得警惕的是，AI 省下来的时间如果只是拿去发更多论文，最后很可能只是把 publish-or-perish 加速到失控。作者甚至直接判断，以论文数量和 h-index 为核心的评价体系正在失效。

作者最后给的方向是让 AI 扩大探索空间，把人的时间留给判断、品味、理解和培养下一代研究者。

以后科研能力可能像「你会不会驾驭一支极快的 AI 研究团队」，而不是一个人能亲手完成多少步骤。

现在顶尖大学里教 Agent，已经开始一路教到 GPU 了。

非常推荐 Harvard 的 CS2680 Modern AI Systems 。课程从 Claude Code、Agent Loop、Eval 和 Token 成本开始，一路往下做到模型部署、Routing、KV Cache、量化和 speculative decoding。

作业设计也很有巧思，5 个作业都围着同一个 Agent 系统往下拆，先看它怎么工作，再自己搭 Harness，最后一路优化到推理层。

感觉它更像是在回答一个问题：

一个现代 AI Agent，到底是怎么从应用层一路跑到底层系统的？

reviewedPosts.author: sh_reya
reviewedPosts.text:
Since the labels are known up front, Quail stores them in a trie and constrains decoding to paths in the trie. Quail stops decoding as soon as only one label is left, instead of decoding the full label. Quail also packs these few decode steps into the same forward passes as the prefill of other documents, so the GPU stays busy. 

On 12 classification queries, Quail is ~1.8x faster than a vLLM baseline!

reviewedPosts.text: To answer this, let's first look at what classification needs. Classification is one of the most common AI-SQL operations. Given a set of documents and a list of labels, the goal is to pick the label that best fits each document. E.g., a support team might sort every incoming message into "billing", "refund request", "shipping delay", and so on. Importantly, the full list of labels is known before the query runs.

New blog post with @charles_irl on how Quail classifies documents with LLMs ~1.8x faster than baselines!! https://t.co/42QNTsdmv8

Most systems classify a document by asking an inference engine to generate the label as free text, and then parsing the labels out of the responses. But the LLM generates text one token at a time, and each of these decode steps is memory-bound, so the GPU sits mostly idle. How can we use the GPU better? 👇
